title: GameXpert-Bench: How Far Are Coding Agents from Expert Game Development?
abstract: arXiv:2608.21833v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs) can operate as coding agents that build complete games from natural language requests. Game development is especially demanding because program logic, visual and audio content, interfaces, interaction and playability must function together in one executable artifact. Measuring this capability therefore requires evaluation of both game product and the development process. Existing benchmarks often assess the game development capabilities of LLMs by evaluating the final artifact or an isolated development stage. Our analysis of complete human-agent development trajectories identifies three stages that together span the lifecycle of game development with a coding agent: initial game generation, bug diagnosis and repair, and optimization over multiple turns. tldr: 本文提出了GameXpert-Bench基准，通过三个互补轨道（初始生成、缺陷修复、多轮优化）全面评估编程代理在游戏开发全生命周期中的能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces GameXpert-Bench, a benchmark with three complementary tracks (initial generation, bug repair, and multi-turn optimization) to comprehensively evaluate coding agents' capabilities across the full game development lifecycle.
